chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Al Nahdy, from Al Husayn, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who visits his brother for the Sake of Allah, Allah Mighty and Majestic Says: “It is I you have visited, and your Reward is upon Me, and I shall not be Pleased for you as a Reward, (anything) less than the Paradise”.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting a brother for the sake of Allah?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to emphasize that visiting a brother in faith is an act of divine worship where the visitor is directly addressing Allah. The promise of Paradise as the exclusive reward underscores the high spiritual status of maintaining these bonds, a concept central to Shia jurisprudence on social obligations. This narration reinforces the idea that interpersonal piety is a direct pathway to divine proximity.
